title: Reading a calibration line
caption: Two calibration points, 2.5 kΩ at 20 °C and 2 kΩ at 25 °C, give a gradient of -0.1 kΩ per °C. A resistance of 2.2 kΩ lies between them, so T = 20 + (2.5 − 2.2)/0.1 = 23 °C. Interpolation is safe only inside the calibrated range.
alt: Straight calibration line of thermistor resistance against temperature through (20, 2.50) and (25, 2.00), with a reading of 2.20 kilohms read across to 23.0 degrees.
description: Horizontal axis: temperature in °C; vertical axis: thermistor resistance in kΩ.
The calibration line joins (20 °C, 2.5 kΩ) and (25 °C, 2 kΩ); its gradient is -0.1 kΩ per °C.
Reading across from R = 2.2 kΩ to the line and down to the axis gives 23 °C.

checks.name: 2.20 kΩ corresponds to 23.0 °C on the line
